nodes.name: On Telegram Event
nodes.notes: Native push trigger — telegram calls this workflow the moment the event happens (no polling). Credential: Telegram bot token. Same bot token as the Telegram node (@BotFather → /newbot).

nodes.name: Keep Valid Conversations
nodes.notes: Drops items that fail the condition; only qualifying items continue (no false branch).

options.systemMessage: You are a voice specialist for the chatbots & conversational ai team. Use the attached tools to look up real data before answering — never invent conversation details. Keep answers under 150 words, cite which tool you used, and escalate anything you cannot verify.

nodes.name: Reason & Act (AI Agent)
nodes.notes: The AI brain: reads the input, decides which attached tools to call (and in what order), then composes the answer. Watch out: Every iteration is a billed LLM call. Max Iterations is the cost ceiling. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run.

nodes.name: OpenRouter Chat Model
nodes.notes: Chat model powering the AI step (model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5). Swap providers here without rewiring. Credential: OpenRouter API key. openrouter.ai/keys → create a key.

parameters.toolDescription: Fetch live conversation data from the internal REST API by id or query.

nodes.name: Lookup API Data
nodes.notes: Tool the agent can call to hit the REST API with parameters it chooses at runtime.

nodes.name: Think It Through
nodes.notes: Scratchpad tool: lets the agent reason step-by-step before acting.

parameters.name: score_helper
parameters.description: Compute a quality score for a conversation record.

nodes.name: Custom Logic Tool
nodes.notes: Deterministic code helper the agent can invoke for exact computation.

nodes.name: Run Calculations
nodes.notes: Math tool — keeps arithmetic exact instead of letting the LLM guess.

nodes.name: Conversation Memory
nodes.notes: Conversation memory keyed by session — the bot remembers earlier turns for each user separately.

nodes.name: Shape Agent Output
nodes.notes: Shapes the item: writes answer, confidence. Keeps the schema explicit between stages.

nodes.name: Confident Enough?
nodes.notes: Two-way gate on ={{ $json.confidence }}. TRUE continues the happy path, FALSE takes the alternate branch. Watch out: The false branch carries the non-matching items — wire it deliberately rather than leaving it dangling.

nodes.name: Deliver Answer + Log to Google Sheets
nodes.notes: Appends a new row to 'Conversation Tracker' — a human-readable audit trail that doesn't require opening n8n to inspect. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Escalate to Human Queue
nodes.notes: Sends a Telegram message to the configured chat — the same bot can also receive replies, so this doubles as a two-way ops channel. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Telegram bot token. Message @BotFather on Telegram → /newbot → copy the token.

nodes.name: Join Outcomes
nodes.notes: Rejoins 2 branches into one stream (mode: append) so downstream logic runs once. Watch out: Waits for every configured input. If one branch never produces items, add 'Always Output Data' upstream so this doesn't stall.

nodes.name: Load Previous Snapshot
nodes.notes: Pulls every page from the Notion database — fine for small datasets; add a filter if the database grows large. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Notion integration token. notion.so/my-integrations → New integration → copy the Internal Integration Token.

nodes.name: Compute Drift vs Snapshot
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Compare current metrics with the previous snapshot Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Fold In Enrichment Fields
nodes.notes: Shapes the item: writes enrichedAt, enrichmentSource. Keeps the schema explicit between stages.

nodes.name: Stamp Completion Time
nodes.notes: Stamps completedAt with the current time for auditing.

nodes.name: Persist Run Metadata
nodes.notes: Saves key fields onto the execution record — searchable later in n8n's execution list.

nodes.name: Serialize Run Output (CSV)
nodes.notes: Serializes items to a CSV binary file.

nodes.name: Archive Row Snapshot
nodes.notes: Creates a new page in the Notion database — the title is pulled straight from the item's key field. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Notion integration token. notion.so/my-integrations → New integration → copy the Internal Integration Token.

nodes.name: Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow
nodes.notes: Delegates to a reusable sub-workflow (single-responsibility building block) and waits for its result. Watch out: The sub-workflow needs an Execute Sub-workflow Trigger as its entry point. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run.

nodes.name: Record Sub-workflow Result
nodes.notes: Saves key fields onto the execution record — searchable later in n8n's execution list.

nodes.name: Fingerprint for Idempotency
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Build a stable idempotency key per conversation (djb2 hash, no deps) Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Drop Already-Processed Items
nodes.notes: Cross-execution dedupe: remembers keys it has processed before and drops repeats — the idempotency guard. Watch out: Cross-execution memory persists. After changing the key field, clear stored keys or old keys keep matching.

nodes.notes: Shapes the item: writes runAt, itemCount, status. Keeps the schema explicit between stages.

# Automate an assistant workflow with Telegram without manual work for Voice

**Pattern:** AI Agent · **Level:** Architect · **Trigger:** Webhook

## What it does
Automate an assistant workflow with Telegram without manual work for Voice. It fires the moment an external system calls its webhook.

## Why it exists
Manual voice is slow and error-prone; this workflow makes the process repeatable, monitored and hands-off, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow
On Telegram Event → Keep Valid Conversations → Reason & Act (AI Agent) → Shape Agent Output → Confident Enough? → Deliver Answer + Log to Google Sheets → Join Outcomes → …

## Use it for
- Teams that want to ai agent without manual effort
- Anyone automating voice in customer support
- Replacing a fragile manual process with a reliable workflow

## You get
- Scales without extra headcount
- Has retries and error handling built in
- Improves response time

## Before first run
Connect credentials: API key / bearer for the target API; Google OAuth2 / service account; Notion integration token; OpenRouter API key; Slack OAuth2; Telegram bot token.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Uses an AI Agent, not a fixed Chain, because the assistant must choose which tool answers the question — a Chain would need one hard-coded branch per tool. The 'Confident Enough?' gate after the agent routes low-confidence answers to a human queue instead of shipping an uncertain answer: a little latency traded for not eroding trust.

## Practice exercises

About as deep as this pattern goes — extend it:

1. Add one more tool to the pool with a clear one-line description and watch how the agent decides to use it.
2. Change the confidence threshold on 'Confident Enough?' and see how often answers get escalated to a human.
3. Swap the Think tool for a Vector Store tool wired to a real knowledge base and turn this into RAG.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Telegram bot token**
Same bot token as the Telegram node (@BotFather → /newbot).
_Gotcha:_ A bot supports only one webhook at a time — a second workflow listening on the same bot steals the updates.

**OpenRouter API key**
openrouter.ai/keys → create a key.
_Gotcha:_ One key reaches many models — handy for fallback.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

**Notion integration token**
notion.so/my-integrations → New integration → copy the Internal Integration Token.
_Gotcha:_ Then open the database → ••• → Connections → add your integration, or every call 404s.

**API key / bearer for the target API**
Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.
_Gotcha:_ Store it as a credential, never typed into the node's parameters.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**HTTP node returns 401 or 403**
Cause: Wrong or unscoped credential, or the API expects a header this request isn't sending.
Fix: Verify the key directly with curl first, then confirm the auth type matches what the API documents.

**HTTP node returns 429**
Cause: Rate limited by the provider.
Fix: Raise the wait between calls or lower the batch size. Retries already back off, but they cannot beat a hard quota.

**AI node fails with an auth or quota error**
Cause: API key missing billing, or the per-minute rate limit was hit.
Fix: Confirm the provider account has credit. For rate limits, lower concurrency or switch to a higher-quota model.

**The AI returns the wrong shape or rambles**
Cause: The prompt is under-specified for the task.
Fix: Tighten the System Message: state the role, the constraints, and the exact output format you expect.

**Execution stalls at the Merge node**
Cause: One input branch produced no items, so Merge is still waiting.
Fix: Enable 'Always Output Data' on the node feeding the empty branch.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Failures are also parked in a dead-letter queue for replay. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🤖 AI cluster

Purple nodes form one AI unit: the root node orchestrates, sub-nodes plug in via typed ports (model / memory / tools / parser). Swap the chat model without rewiring anything else. Costs scale with tokens — keep prompts lean and cap iterations.

## 🧹 Data quality

Dedupe/diff steps make re-runs safe: the same input twice will not create duplicate records. If you change the key fields, clear n8n's dedupe memory (node → 'Clear stored keys') before the next run.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your voice process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.
